observation: The oscillation is bounded by envelopes that decay from +/-4 at t=0 to +/-0.001342 at t=4 s. Its angular frequency remains 6 rad/s while the amplitude decays. The phase offset of 60 degrees is converted to pi/3 radians.

caption: p34 2.4 Multiplication of Two Signals: Y(t) and V(t)=Y(t)W(t).
observation: At t=0 both branches of Y(t) equal 2. The negative-time exponential approaches 2, and the positive-time branch decreases linearly to -8 at 10 s. Multiplication by cos(30t) produces rapid oscillations bounded by |Y(t)|.

caption: p37 3.3 Time Inversion: f(t) and f(-t).
observation: The original exponential rises from 0.0821 at -5 s to 0.6065 at -1 s. Time inversion reflects it onto [1,5], where it is exp(-t/2). The reflected curve has the same values in reverse time order.

caption: p38 Exercise (a) Piecewise Signal: defined piecewise x(t).
observation: The signal is zero for t<-4, equals t+2 on [-4,3], and equals t-2 for t>3. At -4 it takes the middle-branch value -2, and at 3 it takes value 5. The right branch starts just after 3 near 1, so there is a jump there.

caption: p38 Exercise (b)(i) x(t-1): time-shifted x(t-1).
observation: The transformation x(t-1) delays the signal by 1 time unit. Its breakpoints move from -4 and 3 to -3 and 4. The branch values are those of x evaluated one unit earlier.

caption: p38 Exercise (b)(ii) x(t/3): time-expanded x(t/3).
observation: The transformation x(t/3) expands the time axis by a factor of 3. Its breakpoints move to -12 and 9. The branch values are evaluated at one-third of the plotted time.

caption: Sampled values for p38 Exercise (b)(ii) x(t/3).

caption: p38 Exercise (b)(iii) x(-t): time-inverted x(-t).
observation: Time inversion reflects the piecewise signal across t=0. The original breakpoints -4 and 3 appear at 4 and -3. The values are obtained by evaluating x at the negative of the plotted time.
